description: S&P Global is a leading provider of transparent and independent ratings, benchmarks, analytics, and data to the capital and commodity markets worldwide. The company delivers markets intelligence through its divisions, including S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Market Intelligence, S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P Global Commodity Insights, S&P Global Mobility, and Sustainable1. These services support decision-making across various sectors, from finance and commodities to sustainability and mobility. With a history dating back to 1860, S&P Global continues to empower customers with the data and insights needed to navigate complex global markets.

title: S&P Global

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Financial Services and Insurance
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say: 

"What makes S&P Global an exceptional place to work is the thoughtful way it invests in its people, often in ways that aren't typical. From Wellness Days and comprehensive wellness benefits that encourage real recharge, to tuition reimbursement that supports continuous learning and growth, employees are genuinely empowered to thrive. A collaborative, inclusive culture and strong commitment to work-life balance are paired with a generous time-off policy that reflects trust and respect. All of this is reinforced by a clear focus on innovation, giving people both the flexibility and the support to do meaningful, forward-thinking work."

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription: A diverse set of high-powered Wall Street players dominate the 13-person board at market information stalwart S&P Global. The New York–based company employs six current or former CEOs as directors, including Douglas Peterson, the company’s chief executive, and the ex-CEOs of Bank of New York Mellon and Accenture. Gay Huey Evans, former chair of the London Metal Exchange, is among S&P Global’s five female directors. Richard Thornburg, the non-executive chair of the board, was formerly the CFO and chief risk officer of Credit Suisse and a non-executive chair of the financial giant. Gregory Washington, president of George Mason University, who has also led research for the NSF, NASA, and Air Force Research Laboratory, rounds out the board’s expertise. He is one of two Black directors, along with Stephanie Hill, executive vice president of rotary and mission systems at Lockheed Martin. In December, S&P Global unveiled a strategic road map for its next growth phase, revealing plans to leverage A.I. and invest in private markets, sustainability, climate, energy transition, credit and risk management, and emerging markets.
